name: Paneer Butter Masala
cuisine: North Indian (Punjabi / Delhi dhaba-restaurant style; originated in New Delhi per Wikipedia)
equipment: Small bowl for soaking cashews (hot water from a kettle or small pan)
Chopping board and knife; spatula or wooden spoon
Measuring spoons (or a regular teaspoon: 1 level tsp is about 5 ml)
Optional sieve for a silky restaurant-smooth gravy; without one, blend a little longer

steps.title: Soak cashews
steps.text: Put 10 g (7–8) cashews in a small bowl and cover with 30 ml hot water.
steps.visualCue: cashews look slightly swollen and softer, and the water turns faintly cloudy
steps.cameraCheck: bowl of cashews submerged in water
steps.videoShot: hot water poured over cashews in a steel katori
steps.watchOut: cold water barely softens them, so the blend stays gritty; use hot (not boiling-on-the-stove) water, and if short of time, soak at least 10 min.

steps.title: Chop onion
steps.text: Roughly chop 40 g (½ small) onion.
steps.visualCue: rough 2 cm pieces; size does not matter, it all gets blended
steps.videoShot: knife cutting onion into chunks
steps.watchOut: very big chunks cook unevenly and leave a raw onion taste in the gravy; keep them under 3 cm.

steps.title: Chop tomatoes
steps.text: Roughly chop 150 g (2 medium) tomatoes, removing the hard stem point.
steps.visualCue: juicy red chunks, firm-ripe, no green patches
steps.videoShot: tomatoes quartered and chopped
steps.watchOut: pale or unripe tomatoes make the gravy sour and dull; if they are pale, add the full ½ tsp sugar in step 19 and taste.

steps.title: Cube paneer
steps.text: Cut 100 g paneer into 2 cm cubes.
steps.visualCue: even cubes that hold their shape
steps.videoShot: paneer block sliced into strips, then cubes
steps.watchOut: very thin pieces crumble when stirred; keep cubes at least 1.5 cm thick.

steps.title: Soften paneer
steps.text: Cover the cubes with warm (not boiling) water and leave them.
steps.tip: this keeps store-bought paneer soft and stops it going rubbery in the curry.
steps.visualCue: cubes submerged, water slightly milky
steps.videoShot: warm water poured over paneer
steps.watchOut: boiling water makes paneer rubbery and crumbly; the water should feel comfortably warm to a finger.

steps.title: Measure spices
steps.text: On a small plate, put ¾ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, ½ tsp coriander powder, a pinch of turmeric, ¼ tsp garam masala, ½ tsp sugar, ⅓ tsp salt and ½ tsp kasuri methi, each in its own heap.
steps.visualCue: separate heaps of spice, within arm's reach of the stove
steps.videoShot: spoon dropping each spice onto the plate
steps.watchOut: measuring while the pan is hot lets spices burn; have everything ready first.

steps.title: Heat oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 1 tsp (5 ml) oil.
steps.visualCue: oil shimmers and flows freely when you tilt the pan
steps.videoShot: oil swirling in the kadai
steps.watchOut: smoking oil is too hot (it tastes bitter); lower the heat and wait 20 seconds.

steps.title: Sauté onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir.
steps.visualCue: onion turns soft and translucent at the edges, smells sweet, not brown
steps.videoShot: onion sizzling as it is stirred
steps.watchOut: brown edges mean the gravy will taste bitter and darker than the usual orange; lower the heat and add a splash of water.

steps.title: Add ginger-garlic paste
steps.text: Add 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste and stir.
steps.visualCue: raw garlic smell fades and turns savoury
steps.videoShot: paste stirred into onions
steps.watchOut: paste sticking and darkening on the pan; keep stirring and add a spoon of water if it catches.

steps.title: Add tomatoes and drained cashews
steps.text: Add the chopped tomatoes and the cashews (drain off the soaking water, but save it).
steps.visualCue: pan full of tomato chunks with cashews mixed through
steps.videoShot: tomatoes and cashews tipped into the pan
steps.watchOut: throwing away the cashew water; it goes into the blender in step 13.

steps.title: Cook tomatoes down
steps.text: Cover and cook on medium-low, stirring every minute or two.
steps.visualCue: tomatoes are completely mushy, skins curling away, and break when pressed with the spatula
steps.cameraCheck: the pan, pressing a tomato with the spatula
steps.videoShot: spatula squashing soft tomato
steps.watchOut: firm tomato pieces left in will make the purée grainy and sour; keep cooking until a piece squashes with no resistance. If it sticks, add 2 tbsp water.

steps.title: Cool the mixture
steps.text: Switch off the heat and tip the mixture onto a plate to cool.
steps.tip: never blend hot food in a sealed jar.
steps.visualCue: warm, no longer steaming hard
steps.cameraCheck: the plate of cooked tomato mixture
steps.videoShot: mixture spread on a steel plate
steps.watchOut: blending piping-hot food in a closed jar; steam can blow the lid off and scald you.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Put the mixture in the small mixer jar with the saved cashew water and blend until completely smooth.
steps.tip: for a restaurant-silky gravy, push it through a sieve (optional).
steps.visualCue: smooth, bright orange-red purée with no flecks of cashew
steps.videoShot: purée pouring off a spoon in a smooth ribbon
steps.watchOut: tiny cashew bits (gritty gravy); blend 30 seconds longer, or push through a sieve.

steps.title: Melt butter
steps.text: Wipe out the kadai, put it on low heat and add 2 tsp (10 g) butter.
steps.visualCue: butter melted and foaming gently, pale yellow
steps.videoShot: butter melting and foaming
steps.watchOut: brown specks or a nutty-burnt smell; butter on too high a heat browns fast, so lower the heat or start again with fresh butter.
steps.funFact: "makhani" means "buttery", from makhan, the Hindi word for butter (Wikipedia, Paneer makhani).

steps.title: Temper bay leaf
steps.text: Add 1 bay leaf to the butter.
steps.visualCue: leaf sizzles gently and smells fragrant
steps.videoShot: bay leaf sizzling in butter
steps.watchOut: a leaf that turns black (burnt, bitter); lift the pan off the heat for a few seconds.

steps.title: Add spice powders
steps.text: Add the chilli powder, coriander powder and turmeric and stir.
steps.tip: keep the heat low. Spices burn in seconds.
steps.visualCue: butter turns deep red; smells toasty, not burnt
steps.videoShot: red butter swirled with the spatula
steps.watchOut: powders darkening to brown-black within seconds, with a sharp acrid smell; if that happens pour the purée in at once, or start again.

steps.title: Add purée
steps.text: Pour in the blended purée straight away and stir.
steps.visualCue: sauce bubbles gently and spits a little
steps.videoShot: purée poured into the red butter
steps.watchOut: hard splattering on a hot pan; lower the heat and part-cover.

steps.title: Cook the gravy
steps.text: Cook on medium-low, stirring often, partly covered (it splutters).
steps.visualCue: gravy darkens a shade, thickens, and tiny drops of butter appear at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: the pan edge showing the butter separating
steps.videoShot: thick gravy bubbling with shiny edges
steps.watchOut: a raw tomato smell or no butter at the edges means it needs a few more minutes; sticking at the bottom means the heat is too high (add 2 tbsp water).

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add the salt and sugar and stir.
steps.visualCue: dissolved; taste is tangy, mildly sweet, mildly spicy
steps.videoShot: salt and sugar sprinkled in
steps.watchOut: too sweet (a common complaint with this dish); stop at ½ tsp sugar, and if it is too sour add a pinch, not a spoon.

steps.title: Loosen with water
steps.text: Add 60–80 ml (about ⅓ cup) water and stir. Bring to a gentle simmer.
steps.visualCue: gravy coats the back of a spoon and drips slowly
steps.cameraCheck: the back of the spoon coated in gravy
steps.videoShot: finger line drawn through gravy on a spoon
steps.watchOut: gravy that is too thick (it clings in a lump) or watery (runs off the spoon like juice); add water 1 tbsp at a time, or simmer 1 more minute.

steps.title: Add paneer
steps.text: Drain the paneer and add the cubes. Stir gently.
steps.visualCue: every cube coated in orange gravy
steps.videoShot: paneer cubes folded into gravy
steps.watchOut: stirring hard, which breaks cubes into crumbs; fold with the spatula instead.

steps.title: Simmer paneer
steps.text: Simmer on low.
steps.visualCue: paneer is warmed through and soft; gravy bubbles lazily
steps.videoShot: slow bubbles around paneer cubes
steps.watchOut: paneer cooked more than about 5 minutes turns tough and chewy, with no rescue; switch off in time.

steps.title: Add kasuri methi
steps.text: Crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan and stir.
steps.visualCue: aroma becomes noticeably "restaurant-like" and slightly bitter-sweet
steps.videoShot: kasuri methi crushed between palms
steps.watchOut: adding it too early or too much (bitter taste); half a teaspoon, late, is enough.

steps.title: Add garam masala
steps.text: Sprinkle in ¼ tsp garam masala and stir.
steps.visualCue: evenly mixed, warm spice smell
steps.videoShot: garam masala sprinkled over
steps.watchOut: too much garam masala overpowers the butter and tomato; do not add a second pinch.

steps.title: Finish with cream
steps.text: Turn the heat off. Swirl in 1 tbsp (15 ml) fresh cream.
steps.tip: adding cream with the heat off stops it splitting.
steps.visualCue: gravy turns a paler, glossy orange
steps.videoShot: white cream swirled through orange gravy
steps.watchOut: white streaks and a grainy, split look when cream goes into boiling gravy; take the pan off the heat first, and whisk in 1 tbsp water to rescue it.

steps.title: Remove bay leaf and plate
steps.text: Take out the bay leaf, spoon the curry into a bowl and top with chopped coriander (optional).
steps.visualCue: glossy orange curry with visible paneer cubes
steps.videoShot: slow pan across the finished bowl
steps.watchOut: leaving the bay leaf in; it is tough and not meant to be eaten.

reasons: paneer gives good protein (about 23 g), calcium and B12, and the tomato base brings lycopene. But fat is high (about 42 g) with about 23 g saturated (a full day's limit), about 93 mg cholesterol and about 830 mg sodium, and there is almost no vegetable beyond tomato and onion. Restaurant versions commonly use 2–4 times the butter and cream, more sugar and salt, and come with butter naan.

researchRating.basis: one of India's most-cooked and most-ordered paneer dishes; at least 15 independent recipe sites and food blogs publish a restaurant-style version (Veg Recipes of India, Swasthi's, Whisk Affair, Archana's Kitchen, Cook with Manali and others), and it is on pure-veg menus across Mumbai. A recurring complaint is that versions can be too sweet or heavy. Star counts and review totals were not visible in this cycle's search snippets, so the 4.6 is carried over from the previous cycle's evidence (Cooking and Me 4.99 from 60 votes, The Endless Meal 4.9 from 62 ratings, HelloFresh 4.0–4.5), not re-verified.

storage: Fridge-safe in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Freezer: up to 1 month (est.), though the paneer turns slightly spongy and the cream may separate. Reheating: gently on the stove on low with 2–3 tbsp water, stirring, until just hot. In the microwave, use 1-minute bursts and stir between. Do not boil hard.
leftoverRemix: Paneer makhani kathi roll. Simmer the leftover curry until thick, mash a few paneer cubes, spread on a warm roti with sliced onion, a squeeze of lemon and green chutney, and roll it up.
burnOff: about 7.7 km of running (at ~70 kcal/km), or about 11 km of brisk walking (at ~50 kcal/km, est.).

navratri.reason: paneer, cream, butter, cashew and tomato are allowed in the common vrat rule set; skip onion, garlic, kasuri methi and garam masala if your family avoids them, and use sendha namak (assumption: the common rule set).

ekadashi.reason: no grains or pulses in the dish; skip onion and garlic (common rule set; family rules on spices vary).

jain.reason: onion, garlic and fresh ginger are roots; use the Jain variant (sonth, no onion, garlic or ginger).

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; filling and high in protein, but heavy for sehri (about 42 g fat, about 830 mg sodium, est.), so eat a small bowl and drink water.

jain.reason: onion, garlic and fresh ginger are root vegetables; drop all three, use dry ginger powder (sonth) and extra tomato and cashew (see Jain variant).

vegan.reason: paneer, butter and cream are dairy; use firm tofu, oil and extra cashew (see Vegan variant).

sattvik.reason: skip onion and garlic and lean on tomato, cashew and ginger (see Sattvik variant).

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, maida, rava or hing in the recipe; if you add hing use a gluten-free one, as most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour. Check the garam masala label for added flour.

dairyFree.reason: paneer, butter and cream are the dairy; use the Vegan variant.
